claims.statement: A discussion form filename must correspond to the category slug, with an announcements YAML path given as an example. The display label is not independently validated as a slug; file existence alone does not establish feature activation, valid contents, or authorization.

The illustrative YAML defines a title prefix and label, markdown explanatory blocks, a required improvements textarea with bash rendering, a required suggestions input, a required dropdown with four project-area choices, and checkboxes with one required option and one optional option. These sample identifiers and choices are not adopted schema requirements; required responses are not verified truth or attestation, and bash rendering is formatting rather than permission to execute user text.

The fragment locates the Discussions tab beneath a repository or organization name and supplies a repository screenshot caption. Navigation and a caption do not prove the feature is enabled, the image has been inspected, or that a user has access.

The fragment locates the category-edit pencil in the Discussions sidebar. This is a UI navigation reference, not a permission grant or observed configuration change; the screenshot image is not reviewed.

The fragment describes editable category emoji, title, description and one of three discussion formats. Its transfer statement explicitly excludes announcements; transfer prerequisites, target visibility and permissions are not supplied, and no migration or category change was performed.

The organization-enabling sequence goes through settings and a version-conditional sidebar label: Code, planning, and automation for FPT/GHEC versus Code and automation for GHES. It selects Enable discussions, a source repository and Save; despite the filename, no disabling sequence is present. The fragment supplies no observed owner entitlement, repository selection, saved configuration or rollout authorization.
